Canned Lion

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What happens to cubs when their days of cuddling for top dollar are over?

Summary:
A tragic incident where an American tourist was mauled to death at Gautengs top tourist destination, the Lion Park has raised some serious concerns.

The park which prides itself on close encounters with adult lion and cubs has long been an accident waiting to happen says experts in lion behaviour. You simply can't habituate young cubs to people and then allow people into their enclosures where they are bored and unafraid. It will at some point end badly.

Another disturbing reality is - what could you do with an endless stream of cubs to keep visitors happy? And what do you do once they are too big and too dangerous to cuddle. Wildlife groups say that they end up dead - as trophies for canned lion hunters.

Permits issues by Gauteng nature conservation show that at least 2 sets of lions were sent to lion hunting establishments in the last 2 years. We are currently trying to get more recent stats.

Another area of concern is the lack of control over these hunts. Nature conservation officials are meant to be present to ensure that the hunt goes off humanely and the the hunters comply with the permit regulations and dont hunt more than what the permit allows. But authorities are short staffed and this rarely happens.

Which of course may explain why the stats for lion hunts don't correlate. There are substantially more trophies listed by the Chinese government than what CITES and the SA govt reflect in their stats. There is also around 3 tonnes of lion bones exported last year, And it seems the numbers keep growing annually,

Food for thought next time you cuddle a cub.

Clear first hunting shots with 4 Paws

...Which are not involved in hunting industry...” Feels like it needs more clarity

Need map of Boskoppie
Quote Ed Hern’s letter. Put it on screen. Script it better.

Use maps for Farm Inn

Check out Kevin Richardson. He was seen at the Lion Park in December.
Say that owners put forward Scott who has only been there for 6 months.
It seems like we are only attacking the Lion park. For balance, establish the other 2. Says they also have petting.
Left out Australian guy bitten on the thigh and the Taiwanese eaten
One of the major tourist attraction in Gauteng but this isn’t Disney. Something needs to happen to these lions later on.
Cant show crossbow hunt all the way. Stop before they shoot.
Don’t use term “export”.
Explain a bit better about lion bone trade

Script the start of the old man and then go to him comparing to Brahman cattle or Chihuahua

2015-06-29 1.30pm

WG AC GM Bern Okereybea

Can’t show lion’s mating
Don’t like Google Earth effect. Too small. Rather a map.
Hunting shot linked to cub petting signs. It seems as if one of the cubs are being hunted.
Fairness to Scott working there for 6 months...take it out.
Explain more about Cajee and who he is. Pro-hunting articles. Bern says she asked him for response
Say: Lion Park in Lanseria has sold 2 sets of lion to Nazeer Cajee who owns to parks in the North West province.
Shot of Devi looking at documents on computer. Don’t show documents people can pause on or smudge it or don’t use at all.
You say 2013 we exposed... but on screen it say 2010?
Shorty du Randt is new in the story. Bern says given right of reply. She phoned him.
Save 4 lions- add in that it’s because of killing lions in captivity prevents killing a dominant make in the wild and maintains the structure of the pride
Change the order around Nazeer kajee... don’t show us him and then Scott
Ed Hern response paragraph. Check script responds to words on screen
Shorten to 12 minutes

Cut some of Kevin’s comments

Legal: Okereyeba

Put in letter: “They are, (the permits) as you will be aware, a matter of public record as they were tabled in the Gauteng Provincial legislature. Okereybea to write letter.”
Response to Joanne Hunny about number of Vietnam rhinos. Bern says asked her. Now saying undisclosed number in script

Script:



IMPORTANT - NOTE OUTRO at end of Script.


Script Lion Hunting.

Courtesy:
Ben Govender VO: 20”
This is Tibet the white lioness who last month launched a deadly attack on American Game of thrones editor, Katherine Chappel during a visit to the lion park. Despite dozens of warning notices – she opened her window to take pictures. The Lion Park’s Scott Simpson explains.

Scott:
She jumped at the window and managed to bite the lady through the window.

VO: 8”
The lioness then made a second lunge, her guide Pierre Potgieter – tried to fight Tibet off.

Scott:
We were then radioed immediately and myself and a colleague then raced up.

VO: 3”
He called the ambulance they arrived within minutes but it was too late.

VO: 5”
Lion wrangler with 30 years experience, Vicky Brooker, offered her take.

Vicky:
They are 80% instinct and 20% IQ. They are not particularly clever. Almost on a daily basis I work with lions and if I break the rules I am going to be lunch.

CU lion VO: 3”
Fear is a big trigger for lions.

Vicky:
They are inquisitive they want to go and see what is going on. Then obviously the woman panicked, so would I, and that panicked body language triggers offtheir instinct.

VO: 7”
Look online and you’ll find videos of lions in a safari parks opening a car door to get a closer look in.

Upsound:

Screaming!

VO: 9”
Lion whisperer Kevin Richardson worked at the lion park for several years says that half tame like those in the park have lost their fear of humans. But even he wouldn’t open his window to lions he doesn’t know.

Kevin:
If I watch Grey’s anatomy on television and I see a guy performing open heart surgery, does that mean tomorrow I can do open heart surgery? No, there is a thing called common sense and people do need to apply it.

VO: 5”
The lion park has since taken extra precautions and limited access to Tibet’s enclosure.

Scott:
This enclosure is still closed to the public for self drives.

VO: 22”
The park has been dogged by controversy. It’s the third time in the past 6 months that they have hit the headlines. In December last year allegations surfaced in an American programme that some of the parks lions were ending up in the hunting trade. In response activists arranged protest action. Director for the Campaign against Canned Hunting, Linda Park believes they wouldn’t be breeding if they didn’t need cubs for petting.


Linda:
For 356 days of the year there are cubs for petting – where do those cubs go?

VO: 5”
For safari parks cubs are a big draw card.

Scott:
It’s a big part of our business I mean we have almost 200 000 visitors every year and the cub petting is a huge part of that.

VO: 13”
We’d been told several times that the park tells sob stories to visitors to explain why the cubs are separated. So we went undercover.

Upsound undercover:
What happened is that the female rejected the cubs and that’s why they are here. And the little girl that one she was raised by her mom until she was 2 and a half months old and then the female actually died.

VO: 2”
But Scott denied this.

Scott:
We’ve certainly never told guests that – we’ve never said these are orphaned lion cubs.

VO: 15”
So what happens to a constant stream of cubs with a 20 year lifespan? Releasing them into the wild isn’t an option.

Vicky:
The only person that is successful in releasing lions into the wild is Walt Disney because it only happens in the movies it’s not a real thing that can happen.

VO:
Over the years the park has sold off many lions. But good homes are few and far between.

Linda:
There are very few sanctuaries, Kevin has said he cannot take any more lions, Lions rock is full, Jacani is full, Drakenstein is full…so where do these lions go?

Kevin:
The lion park has admitted in the past to having sold off lions to unscrupulous people.

VO: 5”
Which is why he bought 28 lions from the park when he left.

Kevin:
Well you can never be sure what the future is if you turn your back and walk away from a facility. But for me in my heart of hearts I know that Ihad to take my family with me.

VO:
On display boards inside the lion park assurances are given that their cubs won’t end up hunted. But allegations kept surfacing so we took a look at the 3 biggest lion parks offering petting in Gauteng – The lion park just outside Johannesburg, the rhino and lion nature reserve in the Cradle of Humankind and farm inn on the outskirts of Pretoria.

Devi link
We’ve been going through a range of permits looking at safari park sales of lions to other provinces and there are serious questionmarks.


VO:
For instance, the lion park sold 2 sets of 15 lions to Nazeer Cajee a breeder who owns two lodges in the North West. In articles online he is pro hunting.

Scott:
They are all still on his property, he bought them from us for exhibition purposes. I think we were last there doing a site inspection in December.

VO:10
Scott provided an affidavit signed by Cajee that claimed the lions were fit and well and would never be sold into hunting.

Devi: What stops Mr Cajee from selling the lion on to someone else?

Scott:
Apart from the affidavit he signs to state that he won’t sell them on to someone else who is involved in the lion hunting industry. If he does then sell them on he has to get them to sign the same affidavit.


Leon longer

Change VO: 28”
According to permits Cajee sold lion to Andre Steyn who has partnered with Randy Westraadt. Randy according to his linked in profile is a leading big game outfitter specializing in lion hunts for the past 20 years – clearly someone had not done their homework.

VO:
In other deals a total of 30 lions had also been sold and traded to Joanne Hulley a wildlife dealer who had previously worked for Riccardo Ghiazza the man at the centre of the Thuli elephant saga. She allegedly also controversially helped his company send an undisclosed number of rhino to Vietnam.

Scott:
She signed an affidavit to say that she won’t sell those lion on to anyone in the canned lion hunting industry or lion hunting in general.

VO: 8
The first 15 were allegedly sent to Pakistan in 2013. We wanted to know where the 15 taken in February were.


Scott:
She took 15, 3 of them have been exported so far the remaining 12 are still in her possession.

Devi: And where did those 3 go?

Scott: I am not sure you will have to check with Joanne.

VO: 14
When we did that with Joanne she claimed she had confidentiality agreements and could not tell us.

Devi:
Joanne’s affidavit is dated December 2014, now that’s quite a long time after the 2013 purchase?

Scott:
Mnnn…I mean, we’ve always had that agreement, I think we obviously just got it in writing at that point.


Devi: So you never had it in writing before that?


Scott:
It was just a verbal sort of understanding that they wouldn’t be sold into hunting,

Add 7 sec

Devi:
This looks like you are covering tracks?

Scott: No, no.

Devi: Mr Cajee’s affidavit is signed 10 days ago, that’s about when we decided to do the story?

Scott: I mean again we want everyone to sign these affidavits with Mr Cajee, all our lions are on his property and again you were invited there to have a look at them, you’ll be able to scan the microchips and see that they are the same lions.

Devi: Can you prove that your lions were not hunted?

Scott:
Well no, which is why we tried to implement all these systems.

VO:
But their systems clearly aren’t working. We established that the other 12 lions that Joanne took are with Shorty Durand – a controversial figure in canned lion hunting circles.. It seems he used Joanne as the middleman on paper to evade detection. Scott assured us that park owners Rodney Fuhr and Whin Booysen are committed to ensuring this never happens again. But the lion park aren’t alone.

maps

VO: 14”
Farm Inn sold several lion to Boskoppies owners Pieter and Ingrad Swart. We exposed Pieter in 2010 when we tried to buy lions for hunting.

Upsound carte blanche 2010
Young males of two years, two and a half years, I can get those for you, two year old, two and a half years old they will be ready for hunting within a year’s time a year and two three months.

Add 2 sec VO: 21”
Farm Inn owned by the Michelatos family responded with a lawyers letter saying they had no comment and reserved their rights. The lion and rhino nature reserve also appears on the permit list several times. Among their sales are a lion sold to Free State lion bone trader JJ van der Westhuizen, as well as lions sold to breeder and hunter Christo Gomes. We called the reserve’s owner Ed Hern.

Phone call:
Ed Hern: You publish whatever story you want. I’m not worried about that you see. We’ve never been involved in canned lion hunting in any case you understand.

VO:
In a follow up letter they placed the onus on the conservation authorities saying they cannot be held responsible for the actions of the purchasers.

VO: 20”
But the bigger issue is the explosion in the number of lion breeders. Hardly surprising when a white lion trophy can fetch as much as 1 million rand and a tawny lion around R300 000.
When the Cook report first exposed the canned hunting in 1997, with shocking images of a lioness shot in front of her cubs, activists estimated we had 1000 lions in captivity – today we have nearly 8000.

Devi:
700 lions are shot for trophies every single year in South Africa. It’s a huge money spinner but many are questioning its appeal in this day and age.

VO: 11”
Some of these lions are still half tame as seen on this video circulating on the internet. Hunters enter an enclosure where a lioness approaches the vehicle.

Linda:
She’s playing she’s running around and obviously tt’s a game. At one stage she rolls over and shows her tummy which is a sign of submission, you know she’s quite happy and she gets shot with a bow and arrow from the back of a bakkie.

Kevin:
We call them pseudo hunters because they are not hunting, hunters by definition go out there and physically stalks and goes after his quarry and his qyarry has a chance of fair escape.

VO: 8”
Professor Pieter Potgieter chairman of the predator breeders association says they are trying to clamp down on rogue breeders and hunters.

He says the authorities are dropping the ball.

Prof:
Every hunt has to accompanied provincial conservation officer.

Devi: Does that happen?

Prof:
It does not happen. I’d say once in a blue moon he or she would sit in the bakkie while the hunt is going on and he or she has not idea actually of what is going on on the ground.

VO: 11”
It’s an 807 million rand a year industry and his organization is coming up with a plan for ranch lion breeding.

Devi link:
Some people view it as a disturbing shift in thinking while others are welcoming it. Captive lion breeding is being seen a lot like an agricultural entity – a bit like cattle breeding.

VO:
It’s unclear how this will work, will the practice of captive breeding fall under agriculture or will they simply implement some of the principles?


Prof:
Animal health and welfare falls in the mandate of agriculture and once that happens that state department has the right to see what is going on, on the breeding farms.

Linda:
These are not farm animals, they are wild animals. So how can you give a permit and then absolve yourself of any responsibility of how they are taken care of, how the industry is run and if you don’t even go and see any of these hunts and you deny that they are happening.


VO: 7”
Captive lions have long been called the con in conservation because they are bred with little concern for genetics.

Prof:
We are working on that currently by establishing a lion breeders society like you have a stud breeder for association for Brahman cattle or for Chihuahua dogs.

VO:
He believes that shooting captive bred lions actually saves wild lions.

Prof:
If you shoot the main male in the pride, then his second in command comes in and he kills off all the cubs to ensure that his own genes go forward.

Shorten/change VO: 5”
But activists argue with only 8-10 permits to hunt wild lions issued annually this is a flawed argument. The reality is that last week lions were put on the red list they are more threatened than rhinos – we still have 11000 wild rhino and only 2500 lions. Conservations say a life spent in cages , fed in troughs and dragged around is no future for these majestic beasts.


Kevin:
There was a huge outcry when people heard that the lioness at the lion park could be potentially put down and I thought to myself how ludicrous is this, there is a public outcry for this one lioness who has taken a human life but every day in South Africa 3 lions are shot and they did nothing wrong.


Promo 1:

VO: 10
Wildlife activists are lobbying to see lion cub petting stopped believing that many of the cubs land up in trophy hunts…we trawl through the permits in search of answers.

Promo 2:

VO: 4
The spectre of pseudo lion hunting keeps rearing its head..

Linda:

VO: 4
We ask what is the industry doing to clean up its act.



Promo 3:

It’s an 800 million rand industry – with hundreds of lions bred for the bullet.

Devi: Can you say…

Scott: No we can't

VO: We ask - Whats the future for lions in South Africa?


IMPORTANT NOTE:

LINKED to the script in perpetuity

OUTRO: Subsequent to our deadline we received further communication from the Rhino and Lion Park Nature reserve. They asked for proof in relation to our allegations that JJ van der Westhuizen and Christo Gomes are involved in Lion Hunting and indicated that they are totally oblivious to their involvement in this industry. They also confirmed that a white lion cub was sold to JJ Van Der Westhuizen and that other lions were sold to C Gomes and furnished Carte Blanche with the relevant permit numbers. This letter is available in full on our website.

Script Lion Hunting. Courtesy: Ben Govender VO: 20” This is Tibet the white lioness who last month launched a deadly attack on American Game of thrones editor, Katherine Chappel during a visit to the lion park. Despite dozens of warning notices – she opened her window to take pictures. The Lion Park’s Scott Simpson explains. Scott: She jumped at the window and managed to bite the lady through the window. VO: 8” The lioness then made a second lunge, her guide Pierre Potgieter – tried to fight Tibet off. Scott: We were then radioed immediately and myself and a colleague then raced up. VO: 3” He called the ambulance they arrived within minutes but it was too late. VO: 5” Lion wrangler with 30 years experience, Vicky Brooker, offered her take. Vicky: They are 80% instinct and 20% IQ. They are not particularly clever. Almost on a daily basis I work with lions and if I break the rules I am going to be lunch. CU lion VO: 3” Fear is a big trigger for lions. Vicky: They are inquisitive they want to go and see what is going on. Then obviously the woman panicked, so would I, and that panicked body language triggers offtheir instinct. VO: 7” Look online and you’ll find videos of lions in a safari parks opening a car door to get a closer look in. Upsound: Screaming! VO: 9” Lion whisperer Kevin Richardson worked at the lion park for several years says that half tame like those in the park have lost their fear of humans. But even he wouldn’t open his window to lions he doesn’t know. Kevin: If I watch Grey’s anatomy on television and I see a guy performing open heart surgery, does that mean tomorrow I can do open heart surgery? No, there is a thing called common sense and people do need to apply it. VO: 5” The lion park has since taken extra precautions and limited access to Tibet’s enclosure. Scott: This enclosure is still closed to the public for self drives. VO: 22” The park has been dogged by controversy. It’s the third time in the past 6 months that they have hit the headlines. In December last year allegations surfaced in an American programme that some of the parks lions were ending up in the hunting trade. In response activists arranged protest action. Director for the Campaign against Canned Hunting, Linda Park believes they wouldn’t be breeding if they didn’t need cubs for petting. Linda: For 356 days of the year there are cubs for petting – where do those cubs go? VO: 5” For safari parks cubs are a big draw card. Scott: It’s a big part of our business I mean we have almost 200 000 visitors every year and the cub petting is a huge part of that. VO: 13” We’d been told several times that the park tells sob stories to visitors to explain why the cubs are separated. So we went undercover. Upsound undercover: What happened is that the female rejected the cubs and that’s why they are here. And the little girl that one she was raised by her mom until she was 2 and a half months old and then the female actually died. VO: 2” But Scott denied this. Scott: We’ve certainly never told guests that – we’ve never said these are orphaned lion cubs. VO: 15” So what happens to a constant stream of cubs with a 20 year lifespan? Releasing them into the wild isn’t an option. Vicky: The only person that is successful in releasing lions into the wild is Walt Disney because it only happens in the movies it’s not a real thing that can happen. VO: Over the years the park has sold off many lions. But good homes are few and far between. Linda: There are very few sanctuaries, Kevin has said he cannot take any more lions, Lions rock is full, Jacani is full, Drakenstein is full…so where do these lions go? Kevin: The lion park has admitted in the past to having sold off lions to unscrupulous people. VO: 5” Which is why he bought 28 lions from the park when he left. Kevin: Well you can never be sure what the future is if you turn your back and walk away from a facility. But for me in my heart of hearts I know that Ihad to take my family with me. VO: On display boards inside the lion park assurances are given that their cubs won’t end up hunted. But allegations kept surfacing so we took a look at the 3 biggest lion parks offering petting in Gauteng – The lion park just outside Johannesburg, the rhino and lion nature reserve in the Cradle of Humankind and farm inn on the outskirts of Pretoria. Devi link We’ve been going through a range of permits looking at safari park sales of lions to other provinces and there are serious questionmarks. VO: For instance, the lion park sold 2 sets of 15 lions to Nazeer Cajee a breeder who owns two lodges in the North West. In articles online he is pro hunting. Scott: They are all still on his property, he bought them from us for exhibition purposes. I think we were last there doing a site inspection in December. VO:10 Scott provided an affidavit signed by Cajee that claimed the lions were fit and well and would never be sold into hunting. Devi: What stops Mr Cajee from selling the lion on to someone else? Scott: Apart from the affidavit he signs to state that he won’t sell them on to someone else who is involved in the lion hunting industry. If he does then sell them on he has to get them to sign the same affidavit. Leon longer Change VO: 28” According to permits Cajee sold lion to Andre Steyn who has partnered with Randy Westraadt. Randy according to his linked in profile is a leading big game outfitter specializing in lion hunts for the past 20 years – clearly someone had not done their homework. VO: In other deals a total of 30 lions had also been sold and traded to Joanne Hulley a wildlife dealer who had previously worked for Riccardo Ghiazza the man at the centre of the Thuli elephant saga. She allegedly also controversially helped his company send an undisclosed number of rhino to Vietnam. Scott: She signed an affidavit to say that she won’t sell those lion on to anyone in the canned lion hunting industry or lion hunting in general. VO: 8 The first 15 were allegedly sent to Pakistan in 2013. We wanted to know where the 15 taken in February were. Scott: She took 15, 3 of them have been exported so far the remaining 12 are still in her possession. Devi: And where did those 3 go? Scott: I am not sure you will have to check with Joanne. VO: 14 When we did that with Joanne she claimed she had confidentiality agreements and could not tell us. Devi: Joanne’s affidavit is dated December 2014, now that’s quite a long time after the 2013 purchase? Scott: Mnnn…I mean, we’ve always had that agreement, I think we obviously just got it in writing at that point. Devi: So you never had it in writing before that? Scott: It was just a verbal sort of understanding that they wouldn’t be sold into hunting, Add 7 sec Devi: This looks like you are covering tracks? Scott: No, no. Devi: Mr Cajee’s affidavit is signed 10 days ago, that’s about when we decided to do the story? Scott: I mean again we want everyone to sign these affidavits with Mr Cajee, all our lions are on his property and again you were invited there to have a look at them, you’ll be able to scan the microchips and see that they are the same lions. Devi: Can you prove that your lions were not hunted? Scott: Well no, which is why we tried to implement all these systems. VO: But their systems clearly aren’t working. We established that the other 12 lions that Joanne took are with Shorty Durand – a controversial figure in canned lion hunting circles.. It seems he used Joanne as the middleman on paper to evade detection. Scott assured us that park owners Rodney Fuhr and Whin Booysen are committed to ensuring this never happens again. But the lion park aren’t alone. maps VO: 14” Farm Inn sold several lion to Boskoppies owners Pieter and Ingrad Swart. We exposed Pieter in 2010 when we tried to buy lions for hunting. Upsound carte blanche 2010 Young males of two years, two and a half years, I can get those for you, two year old, two and a half years old they will be ready for hunting within a year’s time a year and two three months. Add 2 sec VO: 21” Farm Inn owned by the Michelatos family responded with a lawyers letter saying they had no comment and reserved their rights. The lion and rhino nature reserve also appears on the permit list several times. Among their sales are a lion sold to Free State lion bone trader JJ van der Westhuizen, as well as lions sold to breeder and hunter Christo Gomes. We called the reserve’s owner Ed Hern. Phone call: Ed Hern: You publish whatever story you want. I’m not worried about that you see. We’ve never been involved in canned lion hunting in any case you understand. VO: In a follow up letter they placed the onus on the conservation authorities saying they cannot be held responsible for the actions of the purchasers. VO: 20” But the bigger issue is the explosion in the number of lion breeders. Hardly surprising when a white lion trophy can fetch as much as 1 million rand and a tawny lion around R300 000. When the Cook report first exposed the canned hunting in 1997, with shocking images of a lioness shot in front of her cubs, activists estimated we had 1000 lions in captivity – today we have nearly 8000. Devi: 700 lions are shot for trophies every single year in South Africa. It’s a huge money spinner but many are questioning its appeal in this day and age. VO: 11” Some of these lions are still half tame as seen on this video circulating on the internet. Hunters enter an enclosure where a lioness approaches the vehicle. Linda: She’s playing she’s running around and obviously tt’s a game. At one stage she rolls over and shows her tummy which is a sign of submission, you know she’s quite happy and she gets shot with a bow and arrow from the back of a bakkie. Kevin: We call them pseudo hunters because they are not hunting, hunters by definition go out there and physically stalks and goes after his quarry and his qyarry has a chance of fair escape. VO: 8” Professor Pieter Potgieter chairman of the predator breeders association says they are trying to clamp down on rogue breeders and hunters. He says the authorities are dropping the ball. Prof: Every hunt has to accompanied provincial conservation officer. Devi: Does that happen? Prof: It does not happen. I’d say once in a blue moon he or she would sit in the bakkie while the hunt is going on and he or she has not idea actually of what is going on on the ground. VO: 11” It’s an 807 million rand a year industry and his organization is coming up with a plan for ranch lion breeding. Devi link: Some people view it as a disturbing shift in thinking while others are welcoming it. Captive lion breeding is being seen a lot like an agricultural entity – a bit like cattle breeding. VO: It’s unclear how this will work, will the practice of captive breeding fall under agriculture or will they simply implement some of the principles? Prof: Animal health and welfare falls in the mandate of agriculture and once that happens that state department has the right to see what is going on, on the breeding farms. Linda: These are not farm animals, they are wild animals. So how can you give a permit and then absolve yourself of any responsibility of how they are taken care of, how the industry is run and if you don’t even go and see any of these hunts and you deny that they are happening. VO: 7” Captive lions have long been called the con in conservation because they are bred with little concern for genetics. Prof: We are working on that currently by establishing a lion breeders society like you have a stud breeder for association for Brahman cattle or for Chihuahua dogs. VO: He believes that shooting captive bred lions actually saves wild lions. Prof: If you shoot the main male in the pride, then his second in command comes in and he kills off all the cubs to ensure that his own genes go forward. Shorten/change VO: 5” But activists argue with only 8-10 permits to hunt wild lions issued annually this is a flawed argument. The reality is that last week lions were put on the red list they are more threatened than rhinos – we still have 11000 wild rhino and only 2500 lions. Conservations say a life spent in cages , fed in troughs and dragged around is no future for these majestic beasts. Kevin: There was a huge outcry when people heard that the lioness at the lion park could be potentially put down and I thought to myself how ludicrous is this, there is a public outcry for this one lioness who has taken a human life but every day in South Africa 3 lions are shot and they did nothing wrong. Promo 1: VO: 10 Wildlife activists are lobbying to see lion cub petting stopped believing that many of the cubs land up in trophy hunts…we trawl through the permits in search of answers. Promo 2: VO: 4 The spectre of pseudo lion hunting keeps rearing its head.. Linda: VO: 4 We ask what is the industry doing to clean up its act. Promo 3: It’s an 800 million rand industry – with hundreds of lions bred for the bullet. Devi: Can you say… Scott: No we can't VO: We ask - Whats the future for lions in South Africa? IMPORTANT NOTE: LINKED to the script in perpetuity OUTRO: Subsequent to our deadline we received further communication from the Rhino and Lion Park Nature reserve. They asked for proof in relation to our allegations that JJ van der Westhuizen and Christo Gomes are involved in Lion Hunting and indicated that they are totally oblivious to their involvement in this industry. They also confirmed that a white lion cub was sold to JJ Van Der Westhuizen and that other lions were sold to C Gomes and furnished Carte Blanche with the relevant permit numbers. This letter is available in full on our website.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): What happens to cubs when their days of cuddling for top dollar are over?
metadata.Summary: A tragic incident where an American tourist was mauled to death at Gautengs top tourist destination, the Lion Park has raised some serious concerns. The park which prides itself on close encounters with adult lion and cubs has long been an accident waiting to happen says experts in lion behaviour. You simply can't habituate young cubs to people and then allow people into their enclosures where they are bored and unafraid. It will at some point end badly. Another disturbing reality is - what could you do with an endless stream of cubs to keep visitors happy? And what do you do once they are too big and too dangerous to cuddle. Wildlife groups say that they end up dead - as trophies for canned lion hunters. Permits issues by Gauteng nature conservation show that at least 2 sets of lions were sent to lion hunting establishments in the last 2 years. We are currently trying to get more recent stats. Another area of concern is the lack of control over these hunts. Nature conservation officials are meant to be present to ensure that the hunt goes off humanely and the the hunters comply with the permit regulations and dont hunt more than what the permit allows. But authorities are short staffed and this rarely happens. Which of course may explain why the stats for lion hunts don't correlate. There are substantially more trophies listed by the Chinese government than what CITES and the SA govt reflect in their stats. There is also around 3 tonnes of lion bones exported last year, And it seems the numbers keep growing annually, Food for thought next time you cuddle a cub.
